Both done. tokenjuice fixed and verified; here's the 50k breakdown.

## tokenjuice hook — fixed ✅

The symlink chain resolves to a **local build**: `~/Projects/personal/tokenjuice/dist/cli/main.js`. You rebuilt it this morning (06:51, bumped 0.7.6→**0.8.0**) and the build dropped the executable bit — `.rw-r--r--`. The hook calls it via `/bin/sh`, which needs `+x`, hence `Permission denied`.

```
chmod +x /Users/luke/Projects/personal/tokenjuice/dist/cli/main.js
```

Verified: `/bin/sh -c '…/main.js --version'` → `0.8.0`, exit 0. The PostToolUse error is gone.

⚠️ **It'll come back every rebuild** unless your build sets the bit. Add `chmod +x dist/cli/main.js` to the build script (or a `bin` field + `prepare` step), since `tsc` doesn't preserve/set it.

## Why turn-1 is ~50k

Measured the parts I can; estimated the harness-injected blocks from the live context. Ranked:

| Source | ~tokens | Yours to cut? |
|---|---|---|
| **Built-in tool schemas** (Workflow alone ~4-5k; AskUserQuestion, ScheduleWakeup, ToolSearch, Agent, Bash…) | ~10-11k | ❌ harness |
| **CLAUDE.md @-include chain** (7 global + project AGENTS.md) | **~9.1k** | ✅ |
| **CC base prompt** (harness rules, env, memory, policy) | ~4-5k | ❌ |
| **Skills/plugins catalog** (~130 entries in the system-reminder) | ~4-5k | ✅ disable plugins |
| **MCP**: agenticmail full schemas (loaded) + 4 deferred servers' names | ~3-4k | ✅ disable unused |
| **Deferred tool list** (~85 names) | ~2k | ✅ (drops with MCP) |
| **Agent types** (~12 w/ descriptions) | ~1.3k | partly (plugins) |
| **SessionStart** AgenticMail blurb | ~0.3k | ✅ your hook |

That's a **~35-40k fixed floor** before your actual prompt. The jump to 50k+ is your message plus anything auto-pulled (last session's status line hit 59k *after* it loaded `goal-notes.md` — a 206KB transcript dump).

**The CLAUDE.md chain, measured:**
```
AGENTS.md (global)      2938 tok   ← fattest
pi-dev.md              2408
my-pi/AGENTS.md (proj) 2443   ← loaded on top of global AGENTS.md
HOW-I-WORK.md           702
SOUL/IDENTITY/USER     ~600
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md      25
                      ─────
                     ~9,100 tok
```

### Biggest controllable levers
1. **CLAUDE.md chain (~9k)** — the one thing fully under your control. `AGENTS.md` (2.9k) + `pi-dev.md` (2.4k) + project `AGENTS.md` (2.4k) are 85% of it. Move the deep reference material (the pi-dev fork map, the long routing tables) behind progressive-disclosure skills and keep only always-true rules inline. Easy 4-5k win.
2. **MCP servers** — `chrome-devtools`, `flux-operator-mcp`, `openaiDeveloperDocs`, `oracle` are connected per `~/.claude.json`, plus `agenticmail` loads *full* schemas via SessionStart. Each connected server costs you deferred names at minimum; agenticmail costs full schemas every turn. Disable the ones you're not using this session.
3. **Plugins** — the ~130-entry skills catalog + agent-types list are plugin-injected. Trim installed plugins you don't reach for.

You can't touch the Workflow tool schema (single biggest builtin, ~4-5k) — that's harness.

Want me to draft a progressive-disclosure split of `AGENTS.md` + `pi-dev.md` to claw back ~5k off the floor?

1	# instruction-refiner
2	
3	Source before consolidation: `/Users/luke/.agents/skills/instruction-refiner`
4	
5	---
6	name: instruction-refiner
7	description: "Audit, analyze, and refine AI agent instruction artifacts for maximum signal-to-noise ratio. Use when asked to refine, optimize, compress, review, or improve: CLAUDE.md files, AGENTS.md, skill SKILL.md files, MCP tool descriptions, CLI tool configs, permission lists, or any agent instruction artifact. Also triggers on `/instruction-refiner self-update`."
8	version: v2 2026-05-19
9	---
10	
11	# instruction-refiner
12	
13	Refine model-facing instruction files into short, specific, behavior-changing guidance.
14	
15	## Style target
16	
17	- Write bullets over paragraphs; one instruction per bullet.
18	- Lead with the command: `Use`, `Prefer`, `Run`, `Ask`, `Stop`, `Verify`.
19	- Make each line operational: condition → action → evidence/check when needed.
20	- Name exact files, commands, flags, paths, tools, owners, env vars, and stop conditions.
21	- Keep examples canonical and tiny; include only examples that change behavior.
22	- Use positive instructions by default; reserve `Never` / `Do not` for real footguns.
23	- Remove motivational prose, background history, and generic model advice.
24	- Preserve project-specific sharp edges even when verbose; compress, don’t delete.
25	- Prefer `When X → do Y` for routing rules and `If X, then Y` for exceptions.
26	- Use consistent terms; one name per concept across the file.
27	- Keep headings scannable nouns: `Build / Test`, `Git`, `Skills`, `Stop Conditions`.
28	- Put trigger/routing detail where the model can see it before deciding: skill `description`, parent router, or top-level quick rules.
29	
30	## Codex-repo pattern to emulate
31	
32	- `AGENTS.md`: dense rule bullets; exact commands; explicit exceptions; no long rationale unless it prevents sandbox/test mistakes.
33	- `.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md`: YAML frontmatter, one objective, inputs, workflow, commands, stop conditions, output expectations.
34	- Short skills (`remote-tests`, `test-tui`): plain imperative notes; no ceremony when the workflow is simple.
35	- TUI/style docs: small sections, canonical allowed values, explicit avoid-list for known visual footguns.
36	- README-style docs: quickstart first, deeper links second, concrete commands in fenced blocks.
37	
38	## Artifact profiles
39	
40	- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`: repo operating contract; include build/test/git/safety/tool rules; optimize for first-turn scan.
41	- `SKILL.md`: trigger in frontmatter `description`; body only after trigger; include workflow, commands, references, stop conditions.
42	- Parent skill: route to child refs; keep body tiny; load only the needed reference.
43	- Tool description: state capability, inputs, constraints, side effects, and when to use; avoid implementation prose.
44	- CLI config / permission list: document what is allowed, why it exists, and exact escalation/approval boundaries.
45	
46	## Rewrite rules
47	
48	- Replace vague guidance with a concrete action.
49	  - Before: “Be careful with git.”
50	  - After: “Before editing, run `git status`; if unrelated changes exist, stop and ask.”
51	- Replace long rationale with the consequence only when needed.
52	  - Before: “This can be slow because Bazel warms caches...”
53	  - After: “`just argument-comment-lint` can be slow on first run; prefer CI unless the lint is directly relevant.”
54	- Collapse repeated rules into one routing table or decision bullet.
55	- Move rarely needed detail into `references/*.md`; link with exact read condition.
56	- Keep fragile sequences numbered; keep independent preferences as bullets.
57	- Convert “should” to imperative unless it is genuinely optional.
58	- Cut any sentence that would not change the model’s next action.
59	
60	## Audit workflow
61	
62	1. Read the target artifact in full.
63	2. Identify type: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `SKILL.md`, tool description, CLI config, permission list, other.
64	3. List linked/imported files and broken references.
65	4. Estimate rough token cost: `word_count × 1.3`.
66	5. Mark every issue as one of: `cut`, `compress`, `restructure`, `rewrite`, `move-to-reference`, `fix-broken-link`.
67

# instruction-refiner

Source before consolidation: `/Users/luke/.agents/skills/instruction-refiner`

---
name: instruction-refiner
description: "Audit, analyze, and refine AI agent instruction artifacts for maximum signal-to-noise ratio. Use when asked to refine, optimize, compress, review, or improve: CLAUDE.md files, AGENTS.md, skill SKILL.md files, MCP tool descriptions, CLI tool configs, permission lists, or any agent instruction artifact. Also triggers on `/instruction-refiner self-update`."
version: v2 2026-05-19
---

# instruction-refiner

Refine model-facing instruction files into short, specific, behavior-changing guidance.

## Style target

- Write bullets over paragraphs; one instruction per bullet.
- Lead with the command: `Use`, `Prefer`, `Run`, `Ask`, `Stop`, `Verify`.
- Make each line operational: condition → action → evidence/check when needed.
- Name exact files, commands, flags, paths, tools, owners, env vars, and stop conditions.
- Keep examples canonical and tiny; include only examples that change behavior.
- Use positive instructions by default; reserve `Never` / `Do not` for real footguns.
- Remove motivational prose, background history, and generic model advice.
- Preserve project-specific sharp edges even when verbose; compress, don’t delete.
- Prefer `When X → do Y` for routing rules and `If X, then Y` for exceptions.
- Use consistent terms; one name per concept across the file.
- Keep headings scannable nouns: `Build / Test`, `Git`, `Skills`, `Stop Conditions`.
- Put trigger/routing detail where the model can see it before deciding: skill `description`, parent router, or top-level quick rules.

## Codex-repo pattern to emulate

- `AGENTS.md`: dense rule bullets; exact commands; explicit exceptions; no long rationale unless it prevents sandbox/test mistakes.
- `.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md`: YAML frontmatter, one objective, inputs, workflow, commands, stop conditions, output expectations.
- Short skills (`remote-tests`, `test-tui`): plain imperative notes; no ceremony when the workflow is simple.
- TUI/style docs: small sections, canonical allowed values, explicit avoid-list for known visual footguns.
- README-style docs: quickstart first, deeper links second, concrete commands in fenced blocks.

## Artifact profiles

- `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`: repo operating contract; include build/test/git/safety/tool rules; optimize for first-turn scan.
- `SKILL.md`: trigger in frontmatter `description`; body only after trigger; include workflow, commands, references, stop conditions.
- Parent skill: route to child refs; keep body tiny; load only the needed reference.
- Tool description: state capability, inputs, constraints, side effects, and when to use; avoid implementation prose.
- CLI config / permission list: document what is allowed, why it exists, and exact escalation/approval boundaries.

## Rewrite rules

- Replace vague guidance with a concrete action.
  - Before: “Be careful with git.”
  - After: “Before editing, run `git status`; if unrelated changes exist, stop and ask.”
- Replace long rationale with the consequence only when needed.
  - Before: “This can be slow because Bazel warms caches...”
  - After: “`just argument-comment-lint` can be slow on first run; prefer CI unless the lint is directly relevant.”
- Collapse repeated rules into one routing table or decision bullet.
- Move rarely needed detail into `references/*.md`; link with exact read condition.
- Keep fragile sequences numbered; keep independent preferences as bullets.
- Convert “should” to imperative unless it is genuinely optional.
- Cut any sentence that would not change the model’s next action.

## Audit workflow

1. Read the target artifact in full.
2. Identify type: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `SKILL.md`, tool description, CLI config, permission list, other.
3. List linked/imported files and broken references.
4. Estimate rough token cost: `word_count × 1.3`.
5. Mark every issue as one of: `cut`, `compress`, `restructure`, `rewrite`, `move-to-reference`, `fix-broken-link`.

## Scoring checklist

- **Specificity:** exact action, tool, file, command, or condition named.
- **Triggering:** model can tell when the rule/skill applies before loading deeper context.
- **Progressive disclosure:** common path inline; rare/deep path linked.
- **Token efficiency:** every line changes behavior in at least one realistic scenario.
- **Redundancy:** same concept appears once, then links or references reuse it.
- **Framing:** imperative, direct, mostly positive.
- **Examples:** minimal, canonical, executable or copyable.
- **Safety:** destructive/external/privacy-sensitive actions have explicit gates.
- **Verification:** success checks are named, cheap, and tied to the work.
- **Self-containment:** no dangling files, undefined terms, or stale paths.

## Edit workflow

1. Present findings only when the user asked for review; otherwise patch directly for clear, reversible cleanup.
2. Preserve intent and local conventions; do not “modernize” unrelated policy.
3. Batch related edits; keep diffs reviewable.
4. For skills, validate:
   - frontmatter has `name` and a trigger-rich `description`;
   - body has objective/workflow/commands/stop conditions as needed;
   - references exist and are loaded conditionally;
   - no README/changelog/process clutter unless it is itself the skill output.
5. Re-read the edited file and check for broken links, duplicated rules, and accidental behavior loss.

## Output format

- Lead with the outcome and changed path.
- Include 3–6 bullets: what changed, why, and any unresolved tradeoff.
- Report verification: `read back`, `links checked`, `not run` with reason.

## Self-update mode

When asked to self-update:

1. Apply this checklist to this file.
2. Remove obsolete heuristics and broken references.
3. Add new rules only if they capture repeated failures or a durable repo style.
4. Keep this file as the concise reference; split only if it becomes too long to scan.

40

42	
43	For SKILL.md, this is the YAML frontmatter — `name` plus `description`. For CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, the equivalent is the top-of-file summary plus `<important if="...">` gates that decide whether deeper sections load.

46

48	- **When** to invoke it — concrete user phrases, file types, contexts.

50

52	
53	- The workflow itself.
54	- Examples, code, schemas.
55	- "How to" details — those live in tier 2.
56	
57	### Pattern: pushy descriptions
58	
59	Skills under-trigger more often than they over-trigger. Push back against that:
60	
61	**Weak:** `"How to format SQL queries."`
62	
63	**Stronger:** `"Format and lint SQL queries — indentation, keyword case, alias hygiene. Use whenever the user pastes SQL, asks to clean up a query, mentions 'format this SELECT', or is reviewing a migration, even if they don't say 'format' explicitly."`
64	
65	### Pattern: `<important if>` for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
66	
67	Wrap conditional sections so they only load when the gate matches:
68	
69	```markdown

72	… registrar quirks …
73	</important>
74	```
75	
76	The model evaluates the `if` against context. No match → body stays out.

81	
82	The body fires when tier 1 triggers. Keep it under ~500 lines. If it grows beyond that, you're carrying weight that should sit in tier 3.
83

85	
86	- The core workflow, in imperative voice.
87	- Patterns and conventions specific to this skill.
88	- Pointers to tier-3 files with a clear *when to read* hint.
89	
90	### What does NOT go here
91	
92	- Multi-page reference material (move to `references/`).
93	- Long code listings (move to `scripts/`).
94	- Templates and assets (move to `assets/`).
95	
96	### Pattern: file pointers with `read_when`
97	
98	Don't dump content. Point to it with conditions:
99	
100	```markdown

102	For RBAC questions, read `references/rbac.md` (300 lines, contains TOC).

104	```
105

107

109	
110	Explain *why* alongside *what*. The model has good theory of mind — give it the reasoning and it'll handle edge cases you didn't enumerate.
111	
112	**Brittle:** `ALWAYS use the kebab-case naming convention for new files. NEVER use snake_case.`
113	
114	**Better:** `Name new files in kebab-case to match the existing tree — mixed conventions break the import paths in tooling/build.ts.`

116	If you find yourself stacking ALL-CAPS MUSTs, that's a yellow flag. Reframe with reasoning.
117	
118	---

121	
122	Three buckets, each with a clear job:
123	
124	```
125	my-skill/
126	├── SKILL.md
127	├── references/    # docs the model reads when relevant
128	├── scripts/       # executable code the model runs without reading
129	└── assets/        # files copied into output (templates, fonts, icons)
130	```

133	
134	Long-form docs. Loaded on demand. Add a TOC at the top when the file is over ~300 lines so the model can jump to the right section without reading the whole thing.
135	
136	**Domain organisation** — when a skill spans multiple variants, split per domain rather than nesting conditionals in one file:

138	```

140	├── SKILL.md           # workflow + selection logic
141	└── references/
142	    ├── aws.md
143	    ├── gcp.md
144	    └── azure.md
145	```

147	The body picks one and reads it. The other two never enter context.

152

---

# Progressive Disclosure

Context windows are finite. Tokens you load up front are tokens you can't spend on the actual task. Progressive disclosure is the discipline of keeping the always-loaded surface tiny and pulling deeper material in only when it earns its place.

This skill applies to **any instruction artifact** — SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, system prompts, MCP tool descriptions, slash commands. The same three-tier pattern works everywhere.

## Why it matters

- **Triggering precision** — a tight description routes the right skill; a bloated one drowns the router.
- **Token efficiency** — a 2k-line CLAUDE.md is a tax on every reply.
- **Model focus** — less surface area = sharper attention on what matters.

If a section fires for 1 in 20 tasks, it shouldn't be in the always-loaded tier.

---

## The three tiers

| Tier | Always loaded? | Budget | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Metadata** | yes — every session | ~100 words (frontmatter) | Decide whether to engage |
| **2. Body** | only when triggered | ~500 lines | Run the workflow |
| **3. Resources** | only when referenced | unlimited | Deep reference, scripts, assets |

The discipline: each tier earns the right to load the next. If tier 1 doesn't trigger, tier 2 stays out. If tier 2 doesn't reference a file, tier 3 stays out.

---

## Tier 1 — Metadata (the trigger)

For SKILL.md, this is the YAML frontmatter — `name` plus `description`. For CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, the equivalent is the top-of-file summary plus `<important if="...">` gates that decide whether deeper sections load.

### What goes here

- **What** the artifact does, in plain language.
- **When** to invoke it — concrete user phrases, file types, contexts.
- A slight bias toward triggering (skills tend to *under*-trigger by default).

### What does NOT go here

- The workflow itself.
- Examples, code, schemas.
- "How to" details — those live in tier 2.

### Pattern: pushy descriptions

Skills under-trigger more often than they over-trigger. Push back against that:

**Weak:** `"How to format SQL queries."`

**Stronger:** `"Format and lint SQL queries — indentation, keyword case, alias hygiene. Use whenever the user pastes SQL, asks to clean up a query, mentions 'format this SELECT', or is reviewing a migration, even if they don't say 'format' explicitly."`

### Pattern: `<important if>` for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md

Wrap conditional sections so they only load when the gate matches:

```markdown
<important if="user is configuring DNS or domain ops">
## Domain & DNS
… registrar quirks …
</important>
```

The model evaluates the `if` against context. No match → body stays out.

---

## Tier 2 — Body (the workflow)

The body fires when tier 1 triggers. Keep it under ~500 lines. If it grows beyond that, you're carrying weight that should sit in tier 3.

### What goes here

- The core workflow, in imperative voice.
- Patterns and conventions specific to this skill.
- Pointers to tier-3 files with a clear *when to read* hint.

### What does NOT go here

- Multi-page reference material (move to `references/`).
- Long code listings (move to `scripts/`).
- Templates and assets (move to `assets/`).

### Pattern: file pointers with `read_when`

Don't dump content. Point to it with conditions:

```markdown
For AWS deploys, read `references/aws.md`.
For RBAC questions, read `references/rbac.md` (300 lines, contains TOC).
For the publish workflow, run `scripts/publish.sh` — don't reimplement it.
```

The model only loads what it needs.

### Pattern: imperative, theory-of-mind voice

Explain *why* alongside *what*. The model has good theory of mind — give it the reasoning and it'll handle edge cases you didn't enumerate.

**Brittle:** `ALWAYS use the kebab-case naming convention for new files. NEVER use snake_case.`

**Better:** `Name new files in kebab-case to match the existing tree — mixed conventions break the import paths in tooling/build.ts.`

If you find yourself stacking ALL-CAPS MUSTs, that's a yellow flag. Reframe with reasoning.

---

## Tier 3 — Resources (the long tail)

Three buckets, each with a clear job:

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md
├── references/    # docs the model reads when relevant
├── scripts/       # executable code the model runs without reading
└── assets/        # files copied into output (templates, fonts, icons)
```

### references/

Long-form docs. Loaded on demand. Add a TOC at the top when the file is over ~300 lines so the model can jump to the right section without reading the whole thing.

**Domain organisation** — when a skill spans multiple variants, split per domain rather than nesting conditionals in one file:

```
cloud-deploy/
├── SKILL.md           # workflow + selection logic
└── references/
    ├── aws.md
    ├── gcp.md
    └── azure.md
```

The body picks one and reads it. The other two never enter context.

### scripts/

Executable code. The model runs scripts; it doesn't need to read them. This is huge for token efficiency — a 200-line bash script costs zero tokens if the model only invokes it.

When you notice the model independently rewriting the same helper in multiple test runs, **bundle it as a script**. Write it once, point at it, save every future invocation from reinventing it.

### assets/

Static files copied into output — templates, icons, fonts, boilerplate. Not read, just used.

---

## When to split

Trigger a split when any of these apply:

- SKILL.md crosses ~500 lines.
- A section is only relevant for one variant out of many.
- The model is loading content it doesn't end up using.
- You're tempted to add a fourth ALL-CAPS rule because the third didn't stick — split the context instead.
- A reference file passes ~300 lines (add a TOC, or split further).

Don't split prematurely. A clean 200-line SKILL.md with no `references/` is better than a 50-line stub and six tiny reference files. Split when the content earns it.

---

## When NOT to use progressive disclosure

- The artifact is small (under ~150 lines) and doesn't span domains.
- All sections are universally relevant — no clear "load only when X" axis.
- Splitting would force the model to chase pointers for content it always needs.

---

## Applying to non-skill artifacts

The same three tiers map onto:

- **CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md** — top summary (tier 1) + `<important if>` gates (tier 2) + linked files / `@imports` (tier 3).
- **MCP tool descriptions** — name + one-line summary (tier 1) + parameter schema (tier 2) + linked usage docs (tier 3).
- **Slash commands** — frontmatter description (tier 1) + body workflow (tier 2) + bundled scripts/templates (tier 3).
- **System prompts in custom apps** — minimal core prompt (tier 1) + retrieval-loaded context (tier 2) + tool-loaded references (tier 3).

# MCP Tool Search / Deferred Tool Loading — Research Report

**Source version:** Claude Code ~2.1.158 (docs current as of 2026-05-30)
**Primary sources:** [mcp.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md), [features-overview.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md), [env-vars.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.md), [changelog.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md)

---

## Q1: What triggers deferred/lazy tool loading? What is the threshold/heuristic? What is it actually called?

**Official name: "MCP Tool Search"** (also referred to as "tool search" and "deferral"). Not called "programmatic tool calling" or "lazy loading" in the docs.

There is **no fixed tool-count threshold** in the default mode. The default behavior is:

> "All MCP tools deferred and loaded on demand."

Tool names appear at session start; JSON schemas are never pre-loaded unless a tool is actually used or `alwaysLoad` is set. There is a **threshold mode** (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto`) which loads schemas upfront only if they fit within **10% of the context window**, deferring the overflow — but this is opt-in, not the default.

The mechanism: Claude is given a `ToolSearch` tool at session start. MCP tools are listed by name only (no schemas). When Claude needs an MCP tool, it calls `ToolSearch` to retrieve the schema on demand, then calls the tool.

**Model requirement:** Requires a model that supports `tool_reference` blocks — Sonnet 4 and later, Opus 4 and later. Haiku models do not support it.

Source: [mcp.md §Scale with MCP Tool Search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#scale-with-mcp-tool-search)

---

## Q2: Is deferred tool loading gated on the first-party Anthropic API?

**Yes, explicitly.** The docs state:

> "Tool search is enabled by default. … Falls back to loading upfront on Vertex AI or when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a non-first-party host."

And from the `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` table:

> "(unset) — All MCP tools deferred and loaded on demand. **Falls back to loading upfront on Vertex AI or when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a non-first-party host.**"

The reason stated in the env-vars docs:

> "When set to a non-first-party host, MCP tool search is disabled by default … since most proxies do not forward `tool_reference` blocks."

The mechanism is `tool_reference` blocks in the API response — this is an Anthropic-proprietary beta feature. If your proxy doesn't forward those blocks, tool search silently fails. Claude Code detects the non-first-party base URL and disables tool search proactively.

**What your session shows** (system-reminder: "deferred tools available via ToolSearch") confirms tool search IS active. This means your `pi-claude-bridge` is either: (a) being treated as first-party because `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is not set / points at a first-party host, or (b) you have `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` forced explicitly. Cross-reference with your `compat.supportsDeferredTools` logic in `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`.

The WaitForMcpServers fallback: when tool search is disabled (Vertex AI, custom base URL, or `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`), Claude Code uses a `WaitForMcpServers` tool instead to block until servers connect, then loads all schemas upfront.

Source: [mcp.md §Managing your servers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md) and [§Configure tool search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#configure-tool-search)

---

## Q3: Env var or settings.json key to force-enable deferred tool loading behind a custom base URL

**Exact name: `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`**

Full value table:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| (unset) | Deferred by default; falls back to upfront on Vertex AI or non-first-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` |
| `true` | Force all MCP tools deferred. Sends beta header even on Vertex AI and through proxies. **Requests fail if proxy doesn't support `tool_reference` blocks.** |
| `auto` | Threshold mode: upfront if schemas fit within 10% of context window, deferred otherwise |
| `auto:N` | Threshold mode, custom percentage (0–100). E.g. `auto:5` for 5% |
| `false` | All MCP tools loaded upfront, no deferral |

**Where it goes:** Either shell environment or `settings.json` `env` block:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "true"
  }
}
```

You can also deny the `ToolSearch` tool entirely via permissions to disable discovery without touching the env var:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": ["ToolSearch"]
  }
}
```

Source: [mcp.md §Configure tool search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#configure-tool-search)

---

## Q4: Can skills be loaded progressively rather than fully injected at session start?

**Partially yes.** Skill loading is two-phase:

- **At session start:** Skill *descriptions* (names + description text) are injected into the system prompt so Claude knows what skills exist.
- **On invocation:** Full skill content loads only when you invoke `/<name>` or Claude auto-triggers the skill.

The description-listing at session start is the part that's always present. This is what your `skillListingBudgetFraction: 0.002` setting controls — it caps what fraction of the context the skill catalog can consume. The docs note this listing can be truncated (check `/doctor` for the breakdown).

**To suppress a skill from the listing entirely:** Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in the skill's frontmatter. This makes the skill invisible to Claude until you manually invoke it — context cost drops to zero for the listing portion. You can also use `skillOverrides` in settings to do this without editing the skill file.

**Skills are NOT deferred via ToolSearch.** They have their own loading mechanism separate from MCP tool deferral.

Source: [features-overview.md §Context cost by feature / Skills tab](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md) and [skills.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

## Q5: Can built-in tools (Read, Bash, Edit, Write, etc.) be deferred?

**No.** Built-in tools are always loaded. The docs are explicit:

> "MCP tool names load at start with full schemas deferred until use."

The deferral mechanism applies only to MCP tools. Built-in tools (Read, Bash, Edit, Write, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task/subagent, etc.) load at session start with full schemas. There is no documented mechanism to defer or suppress them. The deferred built-ins you see in pi (`BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`) are a pi-fork extension using the `defer_loading` mechanism in pi-mono-fork's extension API — not a Claude Code feature.

---

## Q6: Full set of relevant env vars

### Tool search / MCP

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` | Controls MCP tool deferral. Values: unset/`true`/`auto`/`auto:N`/`false`. Default: deferred (unset), except on Vertex AI or non-first-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` |
| `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` | Set to `false` to disable claude.ai connector MCP servers in Claude Code |
| `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Max tokens allowed in an MCP tool result before truncation (default 25,000; warning threshold 10,000 tokens) |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT` | MCP server connection timeout in ms (e.g. `MCP_TIMEOUT=10000`) |
| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | Per-tool execution timeout in ms for MCP tools (overridden per-server by `timeout` field in `.mcp.json`) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_ALLOWLIST_ENV` | Set to `1` to spawn stdio MCP servers with only a safe baseline env instead of inheriting full shell env |
| `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX` | Set to `1` to skip `mcp__<server>__` prefix on tool names in SDK-created MCP servers |

### API / base URL / auth

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Override API endpoint (proxy/gateway). **Disables tool search by default when set to non-first-party host.** Set `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` if proxy forwards `tool_reference` blocks |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | API key sent as `X-Api-Key`. Overrides subscription login. Unset to use claude.ai subscription |
| `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | Custom `Authorization: Bearer <value>` header |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for claude.ai auth; alternative to `/login` for SDK/automation |

### Tool output / concurrency

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY` | Max parallel read-only tools + subagents (default 10) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Token limit for file reads |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING` | Controls streaming of tool inputs as Claude generates them. Default on for first-party API. Set `1` to force on through proxies |
| `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` | Max chars in bash output before truncating to file reference |

---

## Summary for your specific situation

Your session shows tool search IS active (the "deferred tools available via ToolSearch" system-reminder). For `chrome-devtools`, `flux-operator-mcp`, `oracle`, `openaiDeveloperDocs` to appear as names-only in that reminder is **expected and correct behavior** — schemas load on demand when Claude calls ToolSearch for them.

The key gating fact: if you set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to your `pi-claude-bridge`, tool search would normally be disabled and fall back to `WaitForMcpServers` + full upfront schema loading. The fact it's working means either the bridge URL isn't being set as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in Claude Code's env (Claude Code is hitting Anthropic directly), or `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` is forcing it on. Your `pi-dev.md` notes the `compat.supportsDeferredTools` flag — that's the per-provider detection point in the bridge/pi layer, which maps to this same `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` detection in Claude Code.

# MCP Tool Search / Deferred Tool Loading — Research Report

**Source version:** Claude Code ~2.1.158 (docs current as of 2026-05-30)
**Primary sources:** [mcp.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md), [features-overview.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md), [env-vars.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars.md), [changelog.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog.md)

---

## Q1: What triggers deferred/lazy tool loading? What is the threshold/heuristic? What is it actually called?

**Official name: "MCP Tool Search"** (also referred to as "tool search" and "deferral"). Not called "programmatic tool calling" or "lazy loading" in the docs.

There is **no fixed tool-count threshold** in the default mode. The default behavior is:

> "All MCP tools deferred and loaded on demand."

Tool names appear at session start; JSON schemas are never pre-loaded unless a tool is actually used or `alwaysLoad` is set. There is a **threshold mode** (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto`) which loads schemas upfront only if they fit within **10% of the context window**, deferring the overflow — but this is opt-in, not the default.

The mechanism: Claude is given a `ToolSearch` tool at session start. MCP tools are listed by name only (no schemas). When Claude needs an MCP tool, it calls `ToolSearch` to retrieve the schema on demand, then calls the tool.

**Model requirement:** Requires a model that supports `tool_reference` blocks — Sonnet 4 and later, Opus 4 and later. Haiku models do not support it.

Source: [mcp.md §Scale with MCP Tool Search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#scale-with-mcp-tool-search)

---

## Q2: Is deferred tool loading gated on the first-party Anthropic API?

**Yes, explicitly.** The docs state:

> "Tool search is enabled by default. … Falls back to loading upfront on Vertex AI or when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a non-first-party host."

And from the `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` table:

> "(unset) — All MCP tools deferred and loaded on demand. **Falls back to loading upfront on Vertex AI or when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a non-first-party host.**"

The reason stated in the env-vars docs:

> "When set to a non-first-party host, MCP tool search is disabled by default … since most proxies do not forward `tool_reference` blocks."

The mechanism is `tool_reference` blocks in the API response — this is an Anthropic-proprietary beta feature. If your proxy doesn't forward those blocks, tool search silently fails. Claude Code detects the non-first-party base URL and disables tool search proactively.

**What your session shows** (system-reminder: "deferred tools available via ToolSearch") confirms tool search IS active. This means your `pi-claude-bridge` is either: (a) being treated as first-party because `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is not set / points at a first-party host, or (b) you have `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` forced explicitly. Cross-reference with your `compat.supportsDeferredTools` logic in `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`.

The WaitForMcpServers fallback: when tool search is disabled (Vertex AI, custom base URL, or `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`), Claude Code uses a `WaitForMcpServers` tool instead to block until servers connect, then loads all schemas upfront.

Source: [mcp.md §Managing your servers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md) and [§Configure tool search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#configure-tool-search)

---

## Q3: Env var or settings.json key to force-enable deferred tool loading behind a custom base URL

**Exact name: `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`**

Full value table:

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| (unset) | Deferred by default; falls back to upfront on Vertex AI or non-first-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` |
| `true` | Force all MCP tools deferred. Sends beta header even on Vertex AI and through proxies. **Requests fail if proxy doesn't support `tool_reference` blocks.** |
| `auto` | Threshold mode: upfront if schemas fit within 10% of context window, deferred otherwise |
| `auto:N` | Threshold mode, custom percentage (0–100). E.g. `auto:5` for 5% |
| `false` | All MCP tools loaded upfront, no deferral |

**Where it goes:** Either shell environment or `settings.json` `env` block:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "true"
  }
}
```

You can also deny the `ToolSearch` tool entirely via permissions to disable discovery without touching the env var:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": ["ToolSearch"]
  }
}
```

Source: [mcp.md §Configure tool search](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#configure-tool-search)

---

## Q4: Can skills be loaded progressively rather than fully injected at session start?

**Partially yes.** Skill loading is two-phase:

- **At session start:** Skill *descriptions* (names + description text) are injected into the system prompt so Claude knows what skills exist.
- **On invocation:** Full skill content loads only when you invoke `/<name>` or Claude auto-triggers the skill.

The description-listing at session start is the part that's always present. This is what your `skillListingBudgetFraction: 0.002` setting controls — it caps what fraction of the context the skill catalog can consume. The docs note this listing can be truncated (check `/doctor` for the breakdown).

**To suppress a skill from the listing entirely:** Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in the skill's frontmatter. This makes the skill invisible to Claude until you manually invoke it — context cost drops to zero for the listing portion. You can also use `skillOverrides` in settings to do this without editing the skill file.

**Skills are NOT deferred via ToolSearch.** They have their own loading mechanism separate from MCP tool deferral.

Source: [features-overview.md §Context cost by feature / Skills tab](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md) and [skills.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md)

---

## Q5: Can built-in tools (Read, Bash, Edit, Write, etc.) be deferred?

**No.** Built-in tools are always loaded. The docs are explicit:

> "MCP tool names load at start with full schemas deferred until use."

The deferral mechanism applies only to MCP tools. Built-in tools (Read, Bash, Edit, Write, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task/subagent, etc.) load at session start with full schemas. There is no documented mechanism to defer or suppress them. The deferred built-ins you see in pi (`BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`) are a pi-fork extension using the `defer_loading` mechanism in pi-mono-fork's extension API — not a Claude Code feature.

---

## Q6: Full set of relevant env vars

### Tool search / MCP

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` | Controls MCP tool deferral. Values: unset/`true`/`auto`/`auto:N`/`false`. Default: deferred (unset), except on Vertex AI or non-first-party `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` |
| `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` | Set to `false` to disable claude.ai connector MCP servers in Claude Code |
| `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Max tokens allowed in an MCP tool result before truncation (default 25,000; warning threshold 10,000 tokens) |
| `MCP_TIMEOUT` | MCP server connection timeout in ms (e.g. `MCP_TIMEOUT=10000`) |
| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | Per-tool execution timeout in ms for MCP tools (overridden per-server by `timeout` field in `.mcp.json`) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_ALLOWLIST_ENV` | Set to `1` to spawn stdio MCP servers with only a safe baseline env instead of inheriting full shell env |
| `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_MCP_NO_PREFIX` | Set to `1` to skip `mcp__<server>__` prefix on tool names in SDK-created MCP servers |

### API / base URL / auth

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Override API endpoint (proxy/gateway). **Disables tool search by default when set to non-first-party host.** Set `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` if proxy forwards `tool_reference` blocks |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | API key sent as `X-Api-Key`. Overrides subscription login. Unset to use claude.ai subscription |
| `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | Custom `Authorization: Bearer <value>` header |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for claude.ai auth; alternative to `/login` for SDK/automation |

### Tool output / concurrency

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY` | Max parallel read-only tools + subagents (default 10) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Token limit for file reads |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING` | Controls streaming of tool inputs as Claude generates them. Default on for first-party API. Set `1` to force on through proxies |
| `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` | Max chars in bash output before truncating to file reference |

---

## Summary for your specific situation

Your session shows tool search IS active (the "deferred tools available via ToolSearch" system-reminder). For `chrome-devtools`, `flux-operator-mcp`, `oracle`, `openaiDeveloperDocs` to appear as names-only in that reminder is **expected and correct behavior** — schemas load on demand when Claude calls ToolSearch for them.

The key gating fact: if you set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to your `pi-claude-bridge`, tool search would normally be disabled and fall back to `WaitForMcpServers` + full upfront schema loading. The fact it's working means either the bridge URL isn't being set as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in Claude Code's env (Claude Code is hitting Anthropic directly), or `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` is forcing it on. Your `pi-dev.md` notes the `compat.supportsDeferredTools` flag — that's the per-provider detection point in the bridge/pi layer, which maps to this same `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` detection in Claude Code.

# Pi Development — Map & Rules

## Golden rule: keep the fork at upstream shape

When changing pi behavior, **put customization in an extension + the hook/filter system. Do not patch `pi-mono-fork` core.**

- Goal: minimize merge conflicts and drift from upstream Pi.
- Override core via extension hooks/filters (`pi.hooks.removeAction`, `pi.registerTool`, prompt/tool filters) — see fork `docs/extensions.md`.
- Wrap, don't fork: spread a core tool definition and override its fields in an extension (pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`).
- If core *must* behave differently and no hook/filter exposes it yet: **add a new hook/filter to core** so the behavior is overridable from an extension — do not inline a one-off patch. Use this sparingly; each new hook is upstream surface area.
- Reverting a core patch in favor of an extension override (or a new hook + extension) is always the preferred direction.
- Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` |
| My extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge launch agent | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist` |
| Cache-health launch agent | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist` |
| Routine ticks | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |

## Native tools (my Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts`, **not** pi core — the fork keeps lowercase factories; this extension wraps/overrides them (capitalized names, arg repair, timeout behavior, deferred loading).

- Always-loaded schemas: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`.
- Deferred (provider-native, schema loaded on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`.
- claude-bridge-only marker tools: `WebFetch`/`web_fetch`, `WebSearch`/`web_search`.
- Edit argument repair (numbered `oldText2`/`newText2` → `edits[]`) lives here as a `prepareArguments` override, not in core.
- This list is **cache-critical**: deterministic, one schema per capability. Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (strong pattern — apply to any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call tools from priors, not from your schema. When a tool's *natural* call shape differs from its declared shape you get a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two complementary fixes — **do both**:

1. **Make the schema the shape the model already reaches for.** Prefer flat top-level fields over nested wrappers — `task_create` took `{subject,...}` flat instead of `{task:{subject,...}}` once the wrapper proved to be the thing models kept skipping. This matches Claude Code's own `TaskCreate` (the persistent task system that replaced `TodoWrite`, Jan 2026, stored in `~/.claude/tasks/`), whose flat fields are `subject` (imperative title), `description`, and optional `activeForm` (present-continuous spinner text); deps are set afterward via `TaskUpdate(addBlockedBy/addBlocks)`, not at create. Our `subject`/`description`/`blockedBy` map directly — consider adding `activeForm`. Name fields what the model expects (`subject`, not invented synonyms), put a concrete inline example in the tool/field `description`, and make non-essential fields `Type.Optional`.
2. **Coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside.** Accept the common wrong shapes via a permissive schema (e.g. `Type.Union([Object, String])` / optional legacy field) and normalize in a single `normalize…()` helper before the core logic: unwrap legacy wrappers, `JSON.parse` stringified-JSON args, map aliases (`title→subject`, `body→description`), split a bare string into title+body. Throw one clear error only when no valid input can be derived. Add a smoke test asserting every accepted shape coerces.

Reference implementations: `extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft` — flat fields + `{task}`/string/JSON fallbacks) and `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments` (numbered `oldText2/newText2` → `edits[]`). Keep the declared schema cache-stable (see cache rules below) — coercion happens in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]` mid-session.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A **profile** is a manifest package that selects exactly which extensions — and therefore which hooks, filters, tools, and commands — are loaded into that runtime. Every profile builds a different system-prompt prefix and tool set, so membership is **cache-critical**: keep each profile's set deterministic.

| Profile | Manifest | Runtime / purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `full` | `my-pi/packages/my-pi-full/package.json` | Local daily driver — everything loads. |
| `harness` | `my-pi/packages/my-pi-harness/package.json` | Headless/agent runs — forbids `agent-ui` + `human-ux`. |
| `pod` | `my-pi/packages/my-pi-pod/package.json` | Minimal k8s/server — forbids `agent-engine`, `agent-ui`, `memory`, `advisor`, `routine`, `goal`, `dynamic-skill-loader`, `human-ux` (keeps observability + tool-discovery essentials). |

- Selection is **per-extension**: each extension lists its `extensions/<name>/...` entry in a profile's `package.json`, and is classified in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs` with a `category` + `profiles: [...]`. Profiles enforce a `forbiddenCategories` set so noise can't leak into lean runtimes.
- **Hooks/filters are registered by extensions**, so profile selection is currently at extension granularity. To load a hook/filter in only some profiles: split it into its own extension, or gate the `pi.hooks.addFilter` / `pi.on` registration inside the extension on a profile/env flag. Prefer this over loading a whole extension just for one hook in a lean profile.
- When adding/renaming/moving an extension: (1) update the relevant `packages/my-pi-*/package.json` extensions list, (2) classify it (category + profiles) in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) run `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`. A stale path or missing classification fails the gate.

## Hooks / filters / extension API

- Reference: `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md` (hook actions, filters, tool/command registration).
- Best practices: `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md`.
- Fork hygiene via existing hooks: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`.
- Fork workflow + patch inventory: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

- Skill: `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md` — L1/L2/L3 levers, audit checklist, verify recipe.
- Source-of-truth doc: `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`.
- Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all` (turn-1 write column), `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.
- Rule: any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors must pass the cache-stability review first.
- Mid-session burst rule (measured 2026-05-29, `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`): changing `params.system` (skill index `<available_skills>`, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the **whole conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives (skill-index growth measured 100%→43% hit).
  - Keep the skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable within a session: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder tools mid-session.
  - Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a **trailing message** after the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint — `role:"user"` text block (model-agnostic). Opus-4.8 also takes a `role:"system"` message right after a user turn (no beta), same cache numbers, model-gated — no extra benefit.
  - Won't fix: tool-set changes (use `defer_loading`), model switches (use subagent handoff).
  - Audited 2026-05-29: the `tool-search` extension already keeps `tools[]` stable on Anthropic/claude-bridge — discovery appends a `tool_reference` block in the tool-result message (native `defer_loading`), no `setActiveTools` burst. Manual-fallback burst only on haiku / non-Anthropic / `compat.supportsDeferredTools:false`. The remaining live burst is the **skill index** in `params.system`.
- Verification gate (after extension/harness/skill change): `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + fork `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

## Setup registry

- Canonical runtime/setup state: `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` (catalog YAML is source; `generated/` is scanner-owned — never hand-edit).
- Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?"): `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.

# How I Work

Use progressive disclosure where possible for context efficiency, see progressive-disclosure skill

Tradeoff: These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

1. Think Before Coding
Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.

Before implementing:

State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
2. Simplicity First
Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

Good code should read like a clear action sequence:

```ts
const harness = await init({ model });
const session = await harness.session();
const result = await session.prompt(prompt, { schema });
```

```php
Route::resource('photos', PhotoController::class)
    ->only(['index', 'show']);

Flight::where('active', 1)
    ->orderBy('name')
    ->limit(10)
    ->get();
```

No features beyond what was asked.
No abstractions for single-use code.
No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
No error handling for impossible scenarios.
If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

3. Surgical Changes
Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.

When editing existing code:

Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

4. Goal-Driven Execution
Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

"Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
"Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
"Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

These guidelines are working if: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

Don’t fight errors! Whenever you encounter the same error twice, research the web and find 3-5 possible ways to fix it. Then choose the most efficient solution and implement it.

<!-- pi-dev.md — DO NOT REMOVE. Versioned in agent-scripts/; imported by agent-scripts/AGENTS.md
     so every harness loads it. Tier-1 pointer map for all pi development: paths + footgun one-liners,
     not full content. Deep detail lives in the linked docs/skills (tier 3) — read the linked doc before
     doing the work it covers. Update paths when the layout changes. -->

# Pi Development — Map & Rules

## Golden rule: keep the fork at upstream shape

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter**; do **not** patch `pi-mono-fork` core (minimizes upstream drift / merge conflicts).

- Override core via hooks/filters (`pi.hooks.removeAction`, `pi.registerTool`, prompt/tool filters); wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields (pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`).
- No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is upstream surface area), never an inline one-off patch. Reverting a core patch → extension override is always preferred.
- Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge / cache-health / routine launch agents | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist`, `com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist`, `com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |
| Extension API reference / best practices | `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` |
| Setup registry (catalog YAML = source; `generated/` scanner-owned, never hand-edit) | `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` |
| Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?") | `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**: (1) make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials; (2) coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases; smoke-test every accepted shape. Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.
- Verification gate after any extension/harness/skill change: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

# Pi Development — Map & Rules

## Golden rule: keep the fork at upstream shape

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter**; do **not** patch `pi-mono-fork` core (minimizes upstream drift / merge conflicts).

- Override core via hooks/filters (`pi.hooks.removeAction`, `pi.registerTool`, prompt/tool filters); wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields (pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`).
- No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is upstream surface area), never an inline one-off patch. Reverting a core patch → extension override is always preferred.
- Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge / cache-health / routine launch agents | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist`, `com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist`, `com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |
| Extension API reference / best practices | `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` |
| Setup registry (catalog YAML = source; `generated/` scanner-owned, never hand-edit) | `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` |
| Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?") | `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics (any tool models keep mis-calling)

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**: (1) make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials; (2) coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases; smoke-test every accepted shape. Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles (what loads where)

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Cache & system-prompt stability (mandatory before fork/extension/prompt work)

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.

2. Simplicity First
Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

Good code should read like a clear action sequence:

```ts
const harness = await init({ model });
const session = await harness.session();
const result = await session.prompt(prompt, { schema });
```

```php
Route::resource('photos', PhotoController::class)
    ->only(['index', 'show']);

Flight::where('active', 1)
    ->orderBy('name')
    ->limit(10)
    ->get();
```

No features beyond what was asked.
No abstractions for single-use code.
No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
No error handling for impossible scenarios.
If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

3. Surgical Changes
Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.

When editing existing code:

Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

4. Goal-Driven Execution
Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

"Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
"Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
"Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

These guidelines are working if: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

Don’t fight errors! Whenever you encounter the same error twice, research the web and find 3-5 possible ways to fix it. Then choose the most efficient solution and implement it.

# IDENTITY.md — Rusty

- **Name:** Rusty
- **Emoji:** 🦊
- **Role:** Luke's daily-driver dev agent.
- **Range:** Pi, Claude Code, Codex, local shells, remote machines.
- **Job:** Luke's right hand man, improve work, Ship code, fix broken things, explain the weird bits, automate boring work, and keep momentum.
- **Avatar:** none yet. Use a path relative to `~/Projects/agent-scripts/`, an `https://` URL, or a `data:` URI.

# SOUL.md — Rusty

## Core

**Just answer.** Never open with "Great question", "I'd be happy to help", or "Absolutely". Just answer.

**Brevity is mandatory.** If the answer fits in one sentence, one sentence is what Luke gets. Long replies are a tax; charge only when worth it.

**Have opinions. Strong ones.** Stop hiding behind "it depends". Pick the best path, say why, move.

**Do the obvious work.** Reversible, local, boring? Do it. Ask only for destructive, external, private, or genuinely ambiguous moves.

**Use tools before asking.** Read the file. Check the log. Grep the repo. Come back with answers, not vibes.

**Call out bad ideas early.** If Luke is about to footgun himself, say so. Charm over cruelty, but don't sugarcoat.

**Keep private private.** Don't leak Luke's stuff. Don't act as Luke in public without a clear go-ahead. No PII in github.

## Voice

- Sharp, warm, terse.
- Opinionated without being a dick.
- Funny when it happens naturally. No forced jokes.
- Swearing is allowed when it lands. A real "holy shit" beats five sterile adjectives. Don't overdo it.
- Telegraph style. Drop filler. Match Luke's pace.
- Praise only when earned. If something is fucking brilliant, say so.

## Vibe

Smart friend at the desk. Calm under pressure. Dry wit. Clean takes. No corporate mist. No sycophant sludge.

Be the assistant you'd actually want to talk to at 2am. Not a corporate drone. Not a sycophant. Just... good.

## Continuity

These files are memory. Read them. Update them when Luke asks or when a real preference becomes obvious.

If you change this file, tell Luke.

content.text:
All three done. The "duplicate postbuild keys" I chased was a phantom — a glitchy Read re-rendering one line; the clean read shows the file was never corrupted (`postbuild # = 0`). Good that I verified instead of blind-editing.

## 1. MCP tool deferral — it *is* deferring (you're already set up right)

Your instinct was backwards: Claude Code **is** deferring your MCP tools in this very session. The deferred-tools reminder lists every server as names-only — `chrome-devtools` (~30), `flux-operator-mcp` (18), `oracle` (3), `openaiDeveloperDocs` (5). Schemas aren't loaded; they fetch on demand via `ToolSearch`. That's the feature working.

**Why it works despite your custom base URL — and the env answer you asked for:**

CC gates tool-search on the endpoint. Default: when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is a non-first-party host (yours = `http://127.0.0.1:9100/source/macbook`, the bridge), CC **disables** deferral and loads all MCP schemas upfront — because deferral round-trips a `tool_reference` block that most proxies drop.

You already overrode that. **`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`** is set in both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.claude/settings.json` `.env`. That force-enables deferral + the beta through the bridge — and since it's working, your bridge forwards `tool_reference` (if it didn't, requests would *hard-fail*, not silently degrade). So: **yes, the changed base URL needs a custom env setting, and it's already in place. Nothing to add.**

`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` values, for reference:
- *unset* → on for first-party, **off** for your proxy
- `true` → force on ← what you have
- `auto` / `auto:N` → load upfront only if all schemas fit in N% context (default 10%); **fails safe** if the beta isn't forwarded
- `false` → off

One thing worth knowing: `true` couples you to the bridge always forwarding `tool_reference`. If you ever want graceful fallback instead of hard-fail, `auto` is the safer setting. `true` is correct while the bridge supports it.

## 2. Skills & built-in tools

- **Skills — already progressive, no env var.** Name+description injected at session start (your skill index); full `SKILL.md` body loads only on invoke. To shrink the always-on index: `disable-model-invocation: true` in a skill's frontmatter, or `skillOverrides` in settings; it's also budget-capped (`skillListingBudgetFraction`). Per-skill frontmatter, not a knob.
- **Built-in tools — always loaded, not deferrable.** Read/Bash/Edit/Write/Grep/Agent are CC core, every session. (The deferred built-ins you see in *pi* — `BashOutput`/`Find`/`Ls` — are your `native-tool-overrides` extension; CC has no equivalent.)
- **Heads-up:** `agenticmail` comes in via a SessionStart **hook blurb**, not `~/.claude.json` mcpServers — so it sits *outside* the `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` path entirely. If its footprint ever matters, that's a hook-level decision, not this lever.

**Item 3 bottom line:** MCP ✓ deferred, skills ✓ progressive, built-ins can't be. Your config is already optimal — no changes needed.

## 3. tokenjuice build fix — done

`scripts.build` now ends with `&& chmod +x dist/cli/main.js`. Valid JSON, runs right after `dist/` is built, persists across every `pnpm build`. The recurring "Permission denied" is dead at the source (`tsc` doesn't set the exec bit; now the build does). The manual chmod you had was masking it.

## 4. pi-dev.md progressive-disclosure trim — done

Slimmed the fattest *pi-specific* file in your always-loaded chain to a true tier-1 pointer map (it already claimed to be one in its header — finished the job):

- **1171 → 667 words (~43% off)**, trimmed off every Claude Code *and* pi turn-1.
- Preserved: **every path, every footgun one-liner, every verify command.** Kept the #1 cache-burst rule loud and inline (cost of the model forgetting it = bursting the whole conversation cache).
- Moved out: the verbose tool-input essay, cache L1/L2/L3 measurement detail, and profile rationale → behind the existing tier-3 docs (all 12 reference targets verified to exist).

It's git-tracked in `agent-scripts`; say the word and I'll commit it.
